answer: A domain name is cheap to buy but impossible to age faster than the calendar. Suppose each identity must publish a signed TXT record on its own domain, registered at least a year before it joins, and earns rewards only while that record resolves. Aged names trade in a thin, watched aftermarket, so a farm buying hundreds drives prices up and leaves a public trail of transfers. Trust cannot grow like a vine overnight: a fresh mirror of an old site fools no registry lookup, and a falcon-eyed auditor can flag batches of names that changed hands the same week.
